llm.title: Send an RPC request with retry

introduction.problem_before: A wallet payment or a mempool broadcast calls RpcClient::send. If the node answers late or not at all, one lost reply fails the whole call with Timeout and the wallet UI shows “offline”.
introduction.change: send tries up to 3 times with exponential backoff (200 ms, doubling, capped at 4 s, plus jitter), then gives up with the new Exhausted error.
introduction.example_before_after: Before: send() → Err(Timeout) after one attempt. After: send() → attempt 1 times out → wait about 200 ms → attempt 2 → Ok.

nodes.label: Attempt: build the request and send once
Retry policy: attempt limit and delays

llm.title: Trigger: callers of send
llm.called_by: a user action in the wallet or the relay (outside the diff)
llm.decides: Nothing here; it builds the request and calls client.send.
llm.why: Shows who reaches the retry loop, in particular a call that is not safe to repeat.

annotations.was: A timeout on this call came back once as Timeout.
annotations.is: The same call may be sent up to 3 times.
annotations.text: broadcast_tx now reaches a retrying send.

llm.title: Attempt: build the request and send once
llm.decides: Counts the attempt; rebuilds the request on every turn.
llm.why: The counter feeds the retry decision; the request is rebuilt because execute consumes it.

annotations.was: Built the request and sent it once.
annotations.is: Builds and sends once per loop turn; the turn count is kept in attempt.

annotations.was: One attempt with the full timeout.
annotations.is: Up to 3 attempts, each with the full timeout.
annotations.text: Every attempt gets the full per-attempt timeout, so the worst case is 3 × timeout plus delays.

llm.title: Outcome of the attempt?
llm.decides: Branches on the result: Ok, Timeout, other error.
llm.why: Only timeouts are retried; every other error keeps the old behaviour.

annotations.was: execute(...).await? returned every error to the caller.
annotations.is: match on the result with three outcomes.

llm.title: Return the response
llm.why: A successful attempt ends the loop at once.

annotations.was: Returned the response.
annotations.is: Returns the response from any attempt.

llm.title: Retry allowed?
llm.decides: Asks RetryPolicy::should_retry(attempt); yes goes to step 6, no goes to step 7.
llm.why: The loop needs a rule for when to stop; the rule is a plain attempt limit.

annotations.was: No retry decision; the timeout went straight to the caller.
annotations.is: Retries while attempt < max_attempts (3). The method of the request is not an input.

annotations.was: A timeout was returned to the caller.
annotations.is: A timeout is retried while attempt < 3, for every method.
annotations.text: mempool::broadcast_tx may submit the same transaction twice if attempt 1 reached the node and only the reply was late.

llm.title: Wait, then try again
llm.why: Spaces the attempts so a briefly overloaded node can recover.

annotations.was: No delay.
annotations.is: Sleeps backoff(attempt): 200 ms doubling, capped at 4 s, plus jitter; then loops to step 2.

llm.title: Give up: Exhausted
llm.decides: Returns the new error instead of Timeout.
llm.why: Callers need to tell a retried failure from a single timeout.

annotations.was: Returned Err(Timeout).
annotations.is: Returns Err(Exhausted { attempts }) once the policy refuses another attempt.

annotations.was: Callers saw Timeout after one attempt.
annotations.is: Callers see Exhausted after the last attempt.
annotations.text: Callers that matched on Timeout no longer see it from send; wallet::fetch_balance maps only Timeout to WalletError::Offline.

llm.title: Other errors returned as before
llm.why: Only timeouts are worth another attempt.

annotations.was: Returned any error.
annotations.is: Returns any non-timeout error at once.

llm.title: Client holds a retry policy
llm.called_by: every caller that builds an RpcClient
llm.decides: Stores RetryPolicy::default() in the new retry field.
llm.why: send needs a policy; new gives every client the default of 3 attempts.

annotations.was: RpcClient had no retry settings.
annotations.is: Every client carries a RetryPolicy, set to the default in new.

llm.title: Retry policy: attempt limit and delays
llm.decides: Allows attempts while attempt < max_attempts; computes the delay before the next attempt.
llm.why: The loop needs a rule for when to stop and how long to wait; both live in one policy value.

annotations.was: No retry rule; util::backoff had only the MAX_ATTEMPTS constant.
annotations.is: should_retry allows another attempt while attempt < max_attempts (3).

annotations.was: No delay rule.
annotations.is: backoff = with_jitter(min(exp_delay(base, attempt), max_delay)).
annotations.text: Jitter is applied after the cap, so one delay can exceed max_delay by up to half (6 s instead of 4 s).

introduction.problem_before: Every RPC call built from RpcConfig::default() waits up to 30 s; the wallet UI froze for 30 s on an unreachable peer (issue #470).
introduction.change: Every attempt now waits at most 5 s.
introduction.example_before_after: Before: timeout = Duration::from_secs(30). After: timeout = Duration::from_secs(5), for each of up to 3 attempts.

llm.title: Default timeout 30 s → 5 s
llm.why: The wallet UI froze for 30 s on an unreachable peer (issue #470).

annotations.was: timeout = 30 s.
annotations.is: timeout = 5 s, for each of up to 3 attempts.

annotations.was: timeout = 30 s.
annotations.is: timeout = 5 s.
annotations.text: sync::fetch_headers relied on the longer wait; CI: sync_headers::slow_peer_2000_headers fails with a timeout after 5 s.

impact.reason: The failing CI test: its peer answers after 12 s, longer than the new 5 s timeout.

llm.title: Affected code: sync::fetch_headers
llm.decides: Requests up to 2000 headers in one reply.
llm.why: Shown because the default timeout reaches it, although the file is not in the diff.

annotations.was: One wait of up to 30 s.
annotations.is: Up to 3 waits of 5 s each, then Exhausted.
annotations.text: A reply that needs 10-20 s now times out on every attempt.

introduction.problem_before: send() could only fail with Timeout or Transport, so callers could not tell “retried and still failed” from one timeout.
introduction.change: A third variant, Exhausted { attempts }, carries the attempt count; send() returns it after the last attempt (flow 1, step 7).
introduction.example_before_after: Before: a match sees Timeout or Transport. After: a match also sees Exhausted { attempts }; wildcard arms swallow it.

pattern_repetitions.description: A wildcard Err(_) arm after explicit RpcError arms swallows Exhausted.

nodes.label: Affected code: wildcard match on send()

llm.title: New error variant RpcError::Exhausted
llm.decides: Adds a variant that carries the attempt count.
llm.why: Callers need to tell “retried and failed” from one timeout.

annotations.was: Two failure variants.
annotations.is: Three; wildcard arms treat the new one as a generic failure.

annotations.was: Two failure variants.
annotations.is: Three failure variants.
annotations.text: Two wildcard match sites outside the diff swallow it (wallet and peers).

impact.reason: Err(_) => {} drops Exhausted: a peer that keeps timing out is never marked failed.

llm.title: Affected code: wildcard match on send()
llm.decides: Maps any other error to WalletError::Rpc.
llm.why: Same pattern × 2; the second site is src/sync/peers.rs:204.

annotations.was: The wildcard arm saw one other error.
annotations.is: The wildcard arm also receives Exhausted.
annotations.text: The user message differs from the Timeout case.

introduction.problem_before: A caller that must not retry used send_once(), next to send().
introduction.change: send_once() is removed; send() is the only entry point and always retries. Side effect: no way is left to send without retry.
introduction.example_before_after: Before: send() and send_once(). After: only send(), which always retries.

llm.title: send_once() removed
llm.called_by: callers that must not retry (none left in this repository)
llm.why: One entry point instead of two.

annotations.was: Two ways to send: with and without retry.
annotations.is: One way, always with retry.
annotations.text: No way is left to send a request exactly once (see flow 1, step 5).

llm.title: Move of backoff helpers util/backoff.rs → rpc/retry.rs

introduction.problem_before: RetryPolicy::backoff (flow 1) calls delay helpers that live in the generic util/backoff.rs.
introduction.change: The helpers move next to the policy, in rpc/retry.rs; 56 of 58 lines move as they were and 2 lines differ.
introduction.example_before_after: Before: JITTER is a tenth, so a delay moves by up to a tenth either way. After: JITTER is a half, so a delay moves by up to half either way.

nodes.label: Module tree: retry in, backoff out

llm.title: Backoff helpers moved
llm.decides: Computes the exponential delay and the jitter.
llm.why: Keeps the helpers next to the policy that uses them.

annotations.was: JITTER is a tenth: a delay moves by up to a tenth either way.
annotations.is: JITTER is a half: a delay moves by up to half either way.

llm.title: Module tree: retry in, backoff out
llm.next: step 1 (the helpers in their new place)
llm.why: The moved file needs its new module path.

annotations.was: util::backoff was a module of util.
annotations.is: rpc::retry is a module of rpc; util::backoff is gone.
